ls_galley_builder.text: It takes months. We start in the autumn. The shape is true Viking, with a dragon head carved fresh each year. All of it, from keel to dragon, is built to burn. That's a funny thing to put your heart into.

There's no heartbreak about it. You build it well because you want it to burn well. A bad galley burns badly. A beautiful galley goes up like a cathedral, and the crowd goes quiet, and then roars. Worth every nail.

ls_jarl_squad.text: The Guizer Jarl and the Jarl Squad lead the procession in Viking dress: helmet, breastplate, shield, axe, cloak. The Jarl himself is chosen years ahead, and the squad is his friends and family. A thousand torches follow in the dark behind.

We march to the field with the galley on a trailer. At the field, the torches are thrown in, and then we sing 'The Norseman's Home'. If you've never heard a thousand people sing in the cold, with a ship on fire, you've missed a trick.

then.text: Still here, still sewing. Do not look at that bolt of canvas. Nobody ever looks at that bolt of canvas, it is its best feature.
Pages? Which pages? I bind in the winter and burn in January, ye'll find me a busy man.

Up Helly Aa is the last Tuesday of January. The squads march with torches, a thousand of them, and the galley goes up in about as long as it takes to say it. We start the next one in February. The torches sort themselves out, mind. The sewing does not.
There is nothing under that canvas, if that is what you are looking at. There is nothing, and I would thank you to stop looking at it.

else.text: Sail canvas, thread, bone folder. Honest tools. What brings ye?
